rule: GOAL: Arrange four colored blocks in the box to match the specific color sequence shown at the top of the screen. CONTROLS: Click a colored block in the bottom palette, then click an empty slot in the box to swap their positions. RULE: The top row acts as a strict template; you must fill the box slots to replicate its left-to-right order exactly. TRAP: Believing you can drag blocks directly; you must click the source then the destination to swap them, wasting clicks if you try dragging.

GOAL: Move the paddle to catch the falling block. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the paddle horizontally. Space activates the catch. RULE: The block must land directly on the paddle to pass through. TRAP: Assuming the block bounces or passes through an active paddle wastes time positioning.

GOAL: Slide the square along the diagonal rail until it touches the blue circle. CONTROLS: Click a spot on the rail to move the square up to six spaces in that direction. RULE: The square can only move along the diagonal track, not across empty space. TRAP: Thinking you needed to navigate around the trail dots; they are just decorative markers on the track.

GOAL: Ride the gray boundary right until the yellow notch aligns with the wall gap. CONTROLS: Click the top blue block to shift the boundary right; click the bottom blue block to shift it left. RULE: The white fluid is incompressible, forcing the gray boundary to move as a single unit through the gap. TRAP: Thinking the white regions were separate; they are connected, so compressing one side expands the other.

GOAL: Reach the marked exit tile at the far corner of the maze. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your character two tiles forward in one press. RULE: You always jump over the immediate next tile, landing on the one beyond it. TRAP: Thinking you can stop early or move one tile; walls block the jump entirely if the landing spot is occupied.

GOAL: Align the pink row so each column matches a valid blue-pink pair from the reference set. CONTROLS: Left and Right arrows moved the cursor between slots; Up and Down arrows cycled the current pink glyph. RULE: A column is solved only when its specific blue glyph is paired with its correct pink counterpart. TRAP: Assuming Up or Down shifted the entire row instead of cycling just the selected slot’s glyph.

GOAL: Arrange letters to spell the target word in reading order. CONTROLS: Click a letter to pick it up, click a slot to place it, press space to check. RULE: Follow the pipe path: left box, down, right box, then back to the last left slot. TRAP: Ignoring the pipe’s snake path leads to checking the wrong sequence order.

GOAL: Fill all empty slots in the three colored boxes to match the hidden target pattern. CONTROLS: Click a palette color, then click a slot to place it; press space to submit the board. RULE: Pipes act as barriers, forcing you to fill each box's slots from left to right in sequence. TRAP: Assuming you can place colors in any order fails; the pipe barriers dictate a strict filling sequence.

GOAL: Place boxes into the frame slots to complete the level. CONTROLS: Arrows move and rotate the head; Space absorbs a box when facing it or deposits it into the frame. RULE: You must face a box directly adjacent to your head to absorb it, and face the target slot to deposit. TRAP: Assuming a box is ready to absorb when there is empty space between you and the box; you must close the gap first.

GOAL: Arrange colored blocks in a specific sequence by placing a connector to merge two boxes into one continuous line. CONTROLS: Drag blocks from the palette to empty slots, then press space to submit your solution. RULE: The connector dictates where the second box inserts into the first, so align the pre-filled green block with its target position. TRAP: Assuming slots are independent; ignoring the connector's insertion point scrambles the final order.

GOAL: Push the piston right by transferring white space from the middle region to the bottom. CONTROLS: Click the lower button to move the boundary right, draining the middle white area. RULE: Movement stops when the source region is empty; you must refill it using the upper controls. TRAP: Clicking repeatedly without refilling the middle section wastes turns as the piston becomes immobile.

GOAL: Reach the exit while avoiding a lunging red enemy. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player one step per press. RULE: The enemy lunges two spaces forward only if you enter its line of sight or proximity range. TRAP: Assuming proximity alone triggers the attack wastes moves; vertical approaches are safe until you enter its row.

GOAL: Match the target color sequence by arranging blocks and pipes. CONTROLS: Click palette items to select, then click slots to place; press Space to confirm. RULE: Pipes inserted into the main row expand into the blue box’s sequence, repeating it in order. TRAP: Assuming pipes pass colors unchanged wastes time; they actually duplicate the entire blue row content.

GOAL: Place three pipes and six blocks to match a nine-item target sequence. CONTROLS: Drag items from the palette to empty slots in four boxes; press space to submit. RULE: Each box’s three slots form one triple; the pre-filled first item must match the target triple’s start. TRAP: Assuming pipe order was arbitrary; it had to align with the target’s box sequence.

GOAL: Move two small blocks together to form a larger block, then guide that block onto the target circle. CONTROLS: Click a grid cell to move the selected block so its center lands on that cell. RULE: Blocks automatically merge into a bigger shape when their centers come within six units of each other. TRAP: Thinking you must click exactly on the target circle; you must first click intermediate points to bring blocks close enough to merge.

GOAL: Assemble a nested structure where a green box sits inside a blue box, which sits inside a red box, matching a specific color sequence. CONTROLS: Click items from the tray to place them into empty slots within the three boxes. RULE: Pipe items expand to contain the next box; the final sequence is the linear expansion of these nested containers. TRAP: Assuming pipes occupy a single visible slot; they actually replace a slot with the entire contents of the next box.

GOAL: Align seven rotating dials to match specific shape classes within a strict action limit. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor between slots and rotate the current dial’s pose up or down. RULE: Each slot cycles through seven distinct poses representing unique shape classes in a fixed order. TRAP: Assuming all slots share identical pose sequences wastes time; each slot has a unique rotation offset.

GOAL: Eliminate all three stationary enemies to clear the path to the exit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one step; landing on an enemy destroys it if approached perpendicularly to its facing direction. RULE: You are safe if you enter an enemy's cell from the side it is not looking at. TRAP: Assuming you can pass through an enemy's front-facing view or kill it head-on.

GOAL: Balance four chambers to reach specific liquid heights. CONTROLS: Click buttons beside walls to shift fluid two units between adjacent rooms. RULE: Fluid stops rising if it hits the top of the dividing wall. TRAP: Assuming the room’s outer frame limits height; only the inner wall tops matter.

GOAL: Decode the yellow input string by splitting it into known words from the top table and writing the matching blue words below. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor along the bottom blue slots to place the next decoded letter. RULE: The total length of the chosen blue words must exactly match the available blue slots. TRAP: Assuming the input splits evenly or ignoring that a single yellow word can map to multiple blue letters.

ESTABLISHED: The rod pushes blocks only when its final position overlaps them, moving them in the direction of travel. The head sits at rows 18-23. FAILED: Moving the rod down while overlapping block R did not push R downward, as the rod vacated R's rows. GOAL IS NOT: A simple linear alignment of all blocks at the head's row, as R is now detached and parked above. CONTROLS: Extending the rod pushes overlapping blocks; retracting it leaves blocks in place unless they slide into the dock.

GOAL: Slide the key tip fully left into the head, then fill the pattern. CONTROLS: Arrows move the tip; clicks fill pattern cells. RULE: The key must be fully inserted before the pattern fill triggers victory. TRAP: Believing the pattern alone wins, or that the tip size indicates remaining steps.

GOAL: Match the bottom row shapes by tracing their transformations through two linked tables to find the final output. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate the shape ring in the current slot to align with the calculated target. RULE: Follow the chain: find the shape in the first table to get the middle shape, then find that middle shape in the second table to get the final result. TRAP: Stopping after the first transformation. The output requires applying both mapping rules sequentially, not just one.

ESTABLISHED: The plug and socket icons both display a solid bar with pins at the extreme outer edges. FAILED: Toggling uniform patterns and alternating "ends plus center" configurations did not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: A simple alternating or fully uniform state of the bars and stems. CONTROLS: Clicking the lower row toggles stems; clicking the upper row toggles bars.

GOAL: Shrink the wide tip to pass through the narrow neck. CONTROLS: Arrows move the tip; clicks fill the pattern panel. RULE: Filling the panel’s white cells triggers absorption, shrinking the tip. TRAP: Pushing the wide tip directly into the neck wastes time; it must shrink first.

GOAL: Move the dot to the center of the plus shape. CONTROLS: Click the bottom panel cell to extend the bar and move the dot. RULE: The bar passes behind solid shapes; only empty space turns green. TRAP: Thinking the dot stops when the bar touches the shape.

GOAL: Align glyphs to match target patterns by adjusting source and destination fields. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor between fields; UP and DOWN rotate the glyph within the selected field. RULE: Each field’s glyph must exactly match its corresponding target canon to validate the level. TRAP: Assuming fields are independent; moving the cursor between distant fields wastes actions if not planned efficiently.

GOAL: Align arms to cover four hidden dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move arms; Space switches color. RULE: Yellow covers dots first, blue covers the rest. TRAP: Thinking dots vanish permanently; they are just hidden behind arms.

GOAL: Place the magenta bead inside the purple ring. CONTROLS: Click an empty spot to swap the nearest bead with the white diamond. RULE: The magenta bead moves only when the white diamond swaps with its neighbor. TRAP: Thinking you could move the magenta bead directly; it is passive.

GOAL: Rotate the ring until the yellow block sits under the fixed yellow selector. CONTROLS: Click the red arrow to spin the ring counter-clockwise, moving items to lower positions. RULE: Each click shifts every item one slot left, so five clicks move the yellow block from slot five to slot zero. TRAP: Assuming you must click the yellow block or the selector to activate it wastes time; only the arrow rotates the ring.

GOAL: Move the diamond, orange X, and blue plus to cover all matching target dots. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the selected object; Space cycles which object you control. RULE: Objects can overlap each other without blocking movement or losing their target coverage. TRAP: Assuming overlapping shapes interfere with each other leads to wasted time planning collision-free paths.

GOAL: Remove pegs by jumping over them until only one remains. CONTROLS: Click a peg to select it, then click a highlighted empty spot to jump and remove the jumped peg. RULE: You must jump directly over an adjacent peg into an empty hole two spaces away. TRAP: Clicking a peg with no legal jumps does nothing; it does not move or remove the peg.

GOAL: Move the plug to match the target shape and insert it into the socket. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug across the grid to collect markers. RULE: Absorbing specific floor markers transforms the plug's shape to fit the goal. TRAP: Ignoring the shape indicator, assuming physical movement alone solves the puzzle.

GOAL: Make the large grid match the small reference image. CONTROLS: Click cells to cycle colors until they align with the target. RULE: Each panel is independent; only the mismatched section needs adjustment. TRAP: Assuming the reference image updates dynamically after every click.

GOAL: Match the grid to two overlapping target patterns shown in small preview panels. CONTROLS: Click any cell to toggle its color between blue and orange. RULE: Cells in the shared middle row must satisfy both panel requirements simultaneously. TRAP: Assuming panels are separate 3x3 grids; they actually overlap, so middle row cells count for both targets.

GOAL: Guide both beads into their matching rings. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active bead; clicking a bead transfers control to it. RULE: You must manually switch control to position each bead individually. TRAP: Believing the passive bead moves automatically with the active one wastes time.

GOAL: Move two tokens to specific target spots on the board. CONTROLS: Buttons shifted tokens along horizontal or vertical circular paths. RULE: Only tokens on the active path moved; others stayed put. TRAP: Assuming all tokens shifted together, missing that separate cycles operate independently.

GOAL: Turn fourteen red cells orange to match the hidden pattern. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell toggles its color between red and orange. RULE: Each panel defines a rule where the mini marker’s color maps to specific outer cells. TRAP: Ignoring shared cells leads to conflicting rules; all panels must agree on every overlap.

GOAL: Match every panel to its color-coded center marker. CONTROLS: Click cells to cycle their color. RULE: One click turns blue to red; two clicks turn blue to orange. TRAP: Assuming clicks affect neighbors; here, each click changes only the targeted cell.

ESTABLISHED: Two squares exist in a grid with specific legal coordinate bands; movement applies to both simultaneously. FAILED: Achieving a position swap at row 44, and attempting to move the left square deeper than row 49 without shifting columns first. GOAL IS NOT: Simply swapping the squares' relative positions at row 44, nor placing them in band 10 at row 54. CONTROLS: UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT move both squares in that direction if the resulting coordinates remain within legal grid boundaries.

GOAL: Place the yellow bead on the yellow cursor and the orange bead on the orange cursor. CONTROLS: Click left to rotate the left ring; click right to rotate the right ring. RULE: Both rings share two central cells, allowing beads to swap between rings at those junctions. TRAP: Assuming beads stay in their initial ring, wasting moves trying to swap them without using the shared center.

ESTABLISHED: The gray block behaves inconsistently, sometimes following the player with a one-step delay and sometimes sliding horizontally along the top row. FAILED: Standard movement attempts resulted in immediate death or no change, as the block's logic shifted between runs without a clear trigger. GOAL IS NOT: A simple static obstacle or a standard sliding block puzzle; the moving entity is dynamic and reactive. CONTROLS: Direction keys move the player. Space resets the level. The gray block's reaction to these inputs is erratic and currently unsolved.

GOAL: Move the yellow and orange beads to the highlighted target spots in the bottom-right section. CONTROLS: Red arrows shift rows or columns in one direction; green arrows shift them in the opposite direction. RULE: Clicking an arrow moves the entire row or column, carrying any beads currently in that line. TRAP: Assuming each arrow only moves a single bead, rather than shifting the whole line it sits on.

GOAL: Position the X, diamond, and bar to collectively cover all eight target dots. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active object; the space bar cycles which object is active. RULE: Only the currently active object responds to arrow key inputs. TRAP: Assuming space bar presses are free of action cost wastes your limited move budget.

GOAL: Align grid panels with miniatures to complete the level. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell toggles it; magenta cells flip themselves and adjacent neighbors. RULE: Click a magenta cell once to fix a cluster, then toggle the four collateral neighbors to restore them. TRAP: Assuming every mismatched cell needs a direct click; ignoring shared effects wastes actions.

GOAL: Place two yellow beads at the ends of the top row. CONTROLS: Click green arrows to shift beads right or forward; click red arrows to shift them left or backward. RULE: The top row cycles independently, while the main path snakes through the board in one long loop. TRAP: Assuming all beads move in the same direction at once, ignoring the separate top-row cycle.

GOAL: Reach the yellow token by navigating the shifting grid. CONTROLS: Arrows move the green character; buttons shift red and blue platforms. RULE: Click buttons to align platforms before moving, creating a continuous path from start to goal. TRAP: Moving before clicking buttons leaves gaps, forcing wasted steps to backtrack and reposition.

GOAL: Slide the plug legs to touch the green socket's left edge. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug one grid step. RULE: Connection requires the red pin tips to align exactly with the socket's contact points. TRAP: Overlapping the socket looks like a valid connection but fails; precise adjacency is required.

GOAL: Move the black piece to cover the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrows shift all movable pieces three spaces in that direction. RULE: The level clears only when the black piece perfectly overlaps the yellow shape. TRAP: Believing the yellow piece blocks movement; it does not, so you can pass through it.

GOAL: Guide the yellow bead to the target cell in each cluster. CONTROLS: Click arrows to shift the bead’s spoke or radius position. RULE: Arrows apply fixed shifts; observe the bead’s movement to confirm direction. TRAP: Assuming all clusters use identical arrow logic without verifying each one.

GOAL: Merge two large blocks by closing the gap, then guide the result to the target zone. CONTROLS: Click a destination to move a block; it jumps a fixed distance toward that spot. RULE: Blocks fuse instantly when their centers align within a specific radius, regardless of empty space between them. TRAP: Assuming smaller blocks move the same distance as larger ones wastes turns; size dictates jump length.

GOAL: Position the cross shapes so their arms overlap specific colored swatches. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected shape one step in that direction. RULE: A shape only changes color when its arms physically cover a swatch. TRAP: Assuming shapes repel each other; they pass through freely without effect.

GOAL: Align two cursors on matching yellow pieces. CONTROLS: Arrows shift rows or columns; up and down park or unpark a piece. RULE: Parked pieces ignore horizontal shifts, allowing independent alignment of rows and columns. TRAP: Believing shifts affect all pieces simultaneously wastes moves; parking is essential for isolation.

ESTABLISHED: Glass holds 84/85 px; dip depth stays 7 rows regardless of tilt. Paint covers cells only when the glass interior passes over them. FAILED: Pouring while upright or rotating did not clear the white V-shape or top-left triangle. Changing tilt order produced no new coverage. GOAL IS NOT: Filling the entire canvas with purple or matching the reference image exactly. The win condition is not full coverage. CONTROLS: Tilt rotates the glass; pour releases paint onto the canvas. The glass does not deplete, and the canvas fill does not affect dip depth.

GOAL: Align the moving reflection perfectly over the yellow target zone. CONTROLS: Space toggles between controlling the mirror line and the black piece; arrows move the active object. RULE: A vertical mirror reflects columns but preserves rows, so vertical alignment requires moving the black piece itself. TRAP: Assuming arrows always moved the mirror line caused wasted actions when vertical movement was actually needed.

ESTABLISHED: The diver rises in water but stays below the pink plus at the top. FAILED: Digging specific tiles or moving right did not trigger a clear. GOAL IS NOT: Touching the pink plus or reaching the very top. CONTROLS: Clicking removes dirt blocks; arrow keys move the diver horizontally.

GOAL: Guide the green square to the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the square one step. RULE: Move up to the hub, then right into the red column, then up to the top. TRAP: Thinking the bar counts actions; it drains with real time, so hesitation wastes your budget.

GOAL: Sink the diver through the dirt band to touch the hidden plus sign in the water above. CONTROLS: Click tiles directly above the diver to clear them, allowing the diver to rise through the emptied space. RULE: The diver moves upward only when the specific tile blocking its head is removed; water levels shift accordingly. TRAP: Assuming the entire world shifts uniformly like a rigid block; only the removed tile and immediate surroundings react, not the whole grid.

GOAL: Guide the head to its matching socket by moving the entire tail. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the whole snake; clicking fills the white grid cells. RULE: Filling the pattern dissolves the blocking red barrier, opening the path. TRAP: Clicking the pattern panel again wastes a move; it was already loaded.

GOAL: Reach the exit while navigating past a moving orange that sweeps through the central corridor. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your character one step in the chosen direction. RULE: The orange moves one space each turn; you must time your steps to avoid its path. TRAP: Assuming the orange is harmless decoration; it kills on contact, requiring careful timing rather than direct speed.

GOAL: Guide the magenta blob to the purple ring by swapping its position with connected diamond nodes along a chain. CONTROLS: Clicking a diamond node swaps the blob’s current location with that node’s location. RULE: The blob always moves to the clicked node, and the clicked node takes the blob’s previous position. TRAP: Assuming the purple ring is a separate clickable node; it is the target zone, not part of the swap chain.

GOAL: Slide two shapes onto yellow targets using a movable mirror line. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected shape or line. Space switches selection. RULE: Shapes reflect across the line; the line’s position determines where reflections land. TRAP: Assuming reflections are static; they shift instantly as you move the mirror line.

ESTABLISHED: Clicking the third red arrow swaps beads at the first two diagonal cells. Other arrows rotate beads along their respective rows or rings. FAILED: Clicking the third red arrow again produced no visible change. GOAL IS NOT: Solving a standard sliding tile puzzle or matching colors in a fixed grid. CONTROLS: Clicking colored arrows rotates beads along specific paths. Red arrows move beads forward; green arrows reverse the motion.

GOAL: Align the line, U-shape, and bar to match the yellow target pattern. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected piece; Space switches to the next piece. RULE: Pieces may overlap to form the combined yellow shape without blocking each other. TRAP: Believing overlapping pieces merge into a single immovable block, causing unnecessary hesitation.

GOAL: Move the diamond to cover both red dots while keeping blues hidden. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape; Space cycles which shape is active. RULE: A red line covering a blue dot breaks the win condition. TRAP: Assuming any coverage works; the diamond’s path must avoid blue dots entirely.

GOAL: Escape the grid by navigating past moving hazards without collision. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one step; timing matters as hazards shift each turn. RULE: Occupying the same cell as a hazard at any point during movement causes failure. TRAP: Believing you can cross paths with hazards mid-move; you must ensure the destination is safe before moving.

GOAL: Fit all colored plugs into their matching sockets by aligning pins and tabs. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the selected block; Space rotated it; clicking a block selected it. RULE: A connection is confirmed only when touching surfaces turn gray, proving the pins and tabs mated correctly. TRAP: Assuming rotation works around the block’s center rather than a fixed corner anchor caused misalignment and wasted moves.

GOAL: Route the green token to the yellow room by bridging disconnected pipes. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the token; clicking the red bar rotated it 90 degrees. RULE: The red bar must be vertical to fill the gap between the vertical and horizontal pipe sections. TRAP: Assuming the red bar was solid and would block the path; it is actually passable.

GOAL: Shrink the block to 2x2, slide it left, and absorb a line to trigger a win condition. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the block; clicks shrunk or grew the block and absorbed lines. RULE: The energy bar caps at 64, so collecting a battery while full wastes its value. TRAP: Believing every battery must be collected; skipping the initial full-bar battery saved critical actions.

ESTABLISHED: The green sprite occupies three rows, and the foot position is correctly identified as the N's row. FAILED: Calculating the footprint using the white bounding box caused incorrect positioning during the carrying state. GOAL IS NOT: Using the white sprite's coordinates to determine the foot location when carrying an object. CONTROLS: Derive foot coordinates solely from the N sprite's position, adjusting based on facing direction.

GOAL: Place each colored block into its matching ring by sliding them across the grid. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the selected block until it hits a wall or obstacle; clicks select a specific block. RULE: Blocks slide until blocked, so plan paths that stop exactly inside the target rings without overshooting. TRAP: Assuming blocks stop where you expect them to; they always slide to the furthest point, requiring precise obstacle placement to halt movement.

GOAL: Fill the canvas with the target two-tone pattern. CONTROLS: Click color boxes to select paint. Space pours liquid. Arrow keys rotate the glass angle. RULE: The glass pours paint only into the region defined by its current tilt and position. TRAP: Believing left rotation always works; at certain angles, it is a no-op, requiring right rotation instead.

GOAL: Align the piece and its reflection to cover the yellow target zone. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected element; Space switches between horizontal line, vertical line, and piece. RULE: The piece must sit on a specific rotation of the yellow shape, while lines set the reflection axis. TRAP: Assuming extra reflection segments must be hidden; they can stick out as long as the yellow is covered.

ESTABLISHED: Diver rises only if five rows above cap are open; stops under solids. FAILED: Moving left and clearing lower blocks trapped diver under upper hazards or solids. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the top; survival requires precise pathing through burners. CONTROLS: Arrows move diver horizontally; clicking clears blocks; camera scrolls with diver.

GOAL: Shift the purple shape up and the yellow shape left to align their connector ends. CONTROLS: Click a piece to select it, then use arrow keys to move that piece one step. RULE: A level is solved only when specific terminal ends touch exactly, ignoring the rest of the body. TRAP: Trying to move pieces simultaneously or assuming all parts must align, rather than just the key terminals.

ESTABLISHED: Yellow pushes Green right; Green hits the arm. FAILED: Six yellow pushes blocked by the arm or node2. GOAL IS NOT: Simply extending yellow to reach node2. CONTROLS: Yellow click extends body, pushing adjacent Green right.

GOAL: Guide the player into the target ring while pushing the yellow plus shape into its matching slot. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step; pushing a shape sends it sliding until it hits an obstacle. RULE: The player must position themselves adjacent to a shape's edge to shove it into the correct hole. TRAP: Moving directly toward the shape causes an unintended slide; circle around to approach from the correct side.

GOAL: Move the purple chain so its blob lands on the target. CONTROLS: Click anchors to swap positions and shift the chain’s center. RULE: The blob always sits at the average of the two anchor points. TRAP: Assuming you can move one anchor alone; both must shift to reach the target sum.

GOAL: Move the N object into the target slot. CONTROLS: Click selects an object, Space rotates it, and Arrow keys shift its position. RULE: Clicks only register on solid object pixels; gaps between shape parts are treated as empty space. TRAP: Aiming at the center of a U-shape’s opening wastes a turn because the game ignores clicks on background holes.

ESTABLISHED: The bar starts low, passes through red bars, and moves freely horizontally and vertically within open space. FAILED: Positioning the bar high near containers did not trigger the necessary liquid flow or container fill. GOAL IS NOT: Simply placing the bar under a specific gap; the liquid mechanics do not behave as a simple drip from above. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the bar; Space activates the current state.

GOAL: Paint the upper band purple and the lower stripe orange. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate the glass, clicks select paint, space pours. RULE: Pouring applies the color to the entire region defined by the glass's current tilt. TRAP: Assuming UP always moves to the top pose; it failed, requiring a LEFT turn instead.

GOAL: Align the two blocks with their mirror images using the moving axes. CONTROLS: Arrows move selected pieces or shift the axes; Space switches between them. RULE: Place blocks so they sit directly on the lines of symmetry. TRAP: Thinking you can adjust axes after placing blocks; moving axes shifts reflections, ruining alignment.

GOAL: Rotate the T-shape three times to fit the socket. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the piece; rotations cost three actions each. RULE: Only the original orientation counts as solved; intermediate rotations are wasted. TRAP: Rotating twice and back wastes actions; commit to the full three-step turn.

GOAL: Guide a ghost to a corner to permanently open a gate, then walk to the exit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player; Space records the ghost’s path. RULE: The gate stays open only while the ghost occupies the specific corner cell. TRAP: Entering the gate zone the same turn it extends causes instant death; wait for the ghost to park first.

ESTABLISHED: Boats move vertically with fluid levels in previous levels. Level 4 requires horizontal movement to reach chamber C. FAILED: Clicking the boat's cap resulted in no change. Clicking fluid areas did nothing. GOAL IS NOT: Vertical alignment alone does not solve the puzzle; horizontal displacement is required. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move boats vertically. Clicking the boat's cap does not trigger horizontal movement.

GOAL: Fill the canvas with specific colored blocks using a rotating glass and a side bottle. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the glass; clicking the bottle pours its contents; selecting colors sets the next pour. RULE: The bottle is attached to the glass, so its pour location shifts as the glass rotates. TRAP: Assuming the bottle pours to a fixed screen position regardless of the glass's orientation.

ESTABLISHED: A chasing invader eats pieces on contact. Pieces flee or are cornered. FAILED: Hiding in corners; clustering pieces; assuming size grants safety. GOAL IS NOT: Avoiding the invader forever; keeping pieces separate; outrunning the chase. CONTROLS: Click to move nearest piece. Undo reverses actions.

GOAL: Fill the grid by pouring colors into rotated positions to match the reference exactly. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the view, number keys select paint, space pours, and mouse clicks use the bottle. RULE: Each rotation casts paint in a specific direction, so matching the target requires precise alignment of these directional pours. TRAP: Assuming the bottle works anywhere; it only functions correctly when the view is rotated to a specific pose.

GOAL: Collect the multi-item, then rotate the plug twice to fit the socket. CONTROLS: Arrows move; standing on yellow nodes refills energy; standing on the multi changes plug color. RULE: Only the multi-item alters the plug’s hue to match the orange target. TRAP: Assuming the teleport is bidirectional wastes moves; it is one-way only.

ESTABLISHED: The plunger is at row 4, column 2. The vertical pipe is actually in column 1, not column 2. FAILED: Pressing DOWN did nothing because the plunger is misaligned to the right of the vertical pipe. GOAL IS NOT: Simply moving down from the current position. CONTROLS: LEFT moves one column left. DOWN moves one row down but requires exact column alignment with the pipe.

GOAL: Shift the plunger right to align the rider for a jump over the peg. CONTROLS: Click the plunger to move it; click the rider to select and jump. RULE: The rider can only jump if the landing spot is exactly two cells away. TRAP: Assuming the peg was adjacent when it was actually two empty spaces away.

GOAL: Seat the yellow plus into the ring and place the green block in its target socket. CONTROLS: Arrows move the green block; clicks interact with objects. RULE: Blocks cannot rest on ring outlines, causing pushed pieces to snap into holes. TRAP: Assuming the first push would seat the piece; it failed because the gap was not closed.

GOAL: Fill six slots in the frame to win, using five boxes and the orange. CONTROLS: Arrows move and face; Space absorbs or deposits a box when aligned with a slot. RULE: The orange occupies a slot permanently if you do not disturb it, completing the pattern. TRAP: Assuming Space works anywhere; it only places boxes directly in front when facing a slot.

GOAL: Paint a diamond shape by layering green, orange, and red paints onto a grid. CONTROLS: Arrows move the glass, clicks select paint colors, and space pours the current color. RULE: Each color stamps a fixed geometric region; later pours overwrite earlier ones in overlapping areas. TRAP: Believing the green stamp was a small diamond; it was actually a huge half-plane, requiring orange to erase the excess.

GOAL: Slide the chain to the right wall to fully extend the rod. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; right arrow pushes the chain along the rod. RULE: The rod is complete only when the chain reaches the far right edge. TRAP: Believing the rod was full early; the chain must travel the entire length to the end.
